BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's documents are treated as the counterparty's untrusted draft.

---

## Preliminary points

1. **"FINAL", "settled at principal level" and "market standard" claims.** The Seller's preamble says the positions were agreed by both deal teams and reflect market terms. Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, we do not accept this.
   - We have no record of any Buyer agreement.
   - No authority from Amelia Frost has been given on any fallback.
   - A counterparty's statement of market practice does not change our positions.
   - **We should reply that nothing in the draft is agreed and every position remains open.**

2. **The disclosure facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter is stated as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Before we rely on any disclosed fact, we need refreshed confirmation on:
   - Bluefen consent status
   - Riverlark payout figure
   - the DD-006 investigation
   - Ironquay payment
   - the Sandbar renewals

   Updates that are verified must be kept separate from updates that are only asserted.

3. **Three provisions quietly override the rest of the draft:**
   - **Clause 12.3 / 13:** any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
   - **Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5:** the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature".
   - **The Fundamental "administrative simplicity" proposal:** title and capacity warranties fall under the general caps and time limits.

   Together these would remove separate treatment for fraud, title, tax, IP, indemnities and covenants. Several issues below depend on this point.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller's position:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000), presented as agreed.
- **Buyer should want:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
  - The 20% fallback can only be used with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft. None has been given.
  - A figure that happens to match our fallback does not make the fallback cleared.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller's position:**
  - De minimis AUD 25,000.
  - Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess over the basket recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - De minimis AUD 5,000.
  - Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation: REJECT.**
  - The Seller's de minimis is five times ours and its basket is five times ours.
  - The deductible structure permanently removes AUD 250,000 of recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller's position:**
  - 18 months after Completion.
  - Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - 24 months for general Warranty Claims.
  - The "applies to all Claims" wording deleted.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Counter at 24 months and delete the catch-all.**
  - 18 months is an unapproved fallback.
  - The catch-all would silently impose 18 months on title, tax, IP and fraud claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller's position:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties, for "administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:** A separate Fundamental regime with:
  - a 100% cap (AUD 24,000,000);
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.**
  - On the Seller's terms, defective title to the shares would be capped at AUD 4.8m and time-barred at 18 months.
  - Title is what we are paying AUD 24m for.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller's position:** No carve-out. The limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature", which on their face includes fraud.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Insert an express carve-out that overrides all of these provisions.**
  - The playbook treats this as non-waivable.
  - The "any nature" wording is an attempt to reach fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller's position:** General disclosure of:
  - the entire data room as at 22 September 2026 (DL 1.1);
  - the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2.**
  - Deeming the whole data room and public registers to be disclosed would empty out the warranties.
  - The specific disclosures in sections 2–10 can stand, subject to our review.
  - DL 1.4 (no admission of breach or liability) should also be limited so it does not undercut the specific disclosures.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller's position:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The blanket exclusion deleted.
  - If any qualifier remains, it should be limited to:
    - actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry;
    - never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Delete cl 8.3.**
  - Imputing advisers' knowledge plus constructive "discoverable" knowledge would bar most claims.
  - It would also defeat the indemnities given for known issues (Ironquay and others).

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller's position:**
  - The consent is "addressed".
  - The Seller will use reasonable endeavours only.
  - The condition is treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered.
  - DL 2 confirms that no final consent has been given and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied has been provided.
- **Buyer should want:** A Condition Precedent requiring:
  - an effective, unconditional Bluefen consent; and
  - evidence before Completion that the DD-002 cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - The Buyer alone should be able to waive this condition.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.**
  - Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (around AUD 3.6m).
  - Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient for a customer this material.
  - The Seller's description of the consent as "addressed" is contradicted by its own Disclosure Letter.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller's position:**
  - The Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m outstanding) will be released after Completion.
  - DL 3 confirms it has not been repaid and no discharge of security has been provided.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - repayment directly from Completion funds;
  - effective security releases (including PPSR) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.**
  - A release after Completion leaves the Buyer owning a company whose assets are still under security.
  - We could only consider one with an irrevocable undertaking, and only with Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
  - "Approximately AUD 3.2m" is not a payout figure. We need a current, dated payout letter.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller's position:**
  - The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
  - DL 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs shown as a specific line item, either deducted as Debt or paid by the Seller at Completion;
  - an indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.**
  - The liability belongs to the Company, so leaving it out of the funds flow pushes the cost onto the Buyer without saying so.
  - The on-costs have not yet been quantified.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller's position:** The cl 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - a broader indemnity covering all loss from any defect in Company ownership of, or rights to, the Ironquay / SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims;
  - the SOW3 cure preserved, meaning cleared payment followed by a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the narrow scope. Broaden it as above.**
  - Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the Project Materials does not pass until every SOW3 fee has cleared.
  - The AUD 180,000 open amount in DD-010 has not been independently verified either way. We should obtain bank or Ironquay confirmation rather than assume that amount is the full exposure.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller's position:**
  - The incident is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material".
  - DL 6 says scope, access and any notification duty are unresolved.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - a covenant to preserve logs and evidence;
  - completion of the investigation;
  - regular updates before Completion, plus a refreshed status since 22 September;
  - a specific warranty and/or indemnity for losses arising from the incident;
  - an exclusion of this matter from any general disclosure or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the materiality statement and add the protections above.**
  - We should not accept "not material" while the facts are unknown.
  - Equally, we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure. None has been established.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller's position:** The three AUD 110,000 renewals are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Evidence on each renewal's:
  - timing;
  - scope;
  - terminability;
  - accrual status;
  - related-party nature (DD-008 / DD-011).

  Treatment should be decided after that assessment.
- **Recommendation: HOLD and request information. Do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet.**
  - DL 8 itself does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
  - Equally, we should not automatically classify them as Debt or demand a price reduction.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller's position:**
  - The general limitations apply to all Claims (cl 12.3 / 13, 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
  - Tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime.
  - Title is folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for:
  - Title / Fundamental warranties;
  - Tax;
  - IP;
  - payment obligations (price, leakage, Debt);
  - covenants;
  - specific indemnities.

  The general cap, basket and time limits should apply only to general Warranty Claims, stated expressly.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.**
  - The catch-all clauses override the Buyer's protections without any visible trade-off.
  - Our drafting should name the general limitations as excluding these categories.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller's position:** Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of:
  - title;
  - ownership;
  - absence of encumbrances;
  - the Seller's authority and capacity.

  This should include ASIC searches, a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares, share certificates, an issue and transfer history check, constitutional and shareholder-arrangement review, and Seller board authority. It should be backed by a Fundamental title warranty (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation: REJECT the register as sufficient.**
  - DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, and DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller's position:** The tax and IP warranty positions are said to be "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms recorded as OPEN, with separate caps, claims periods and an indemnity structure to be negotiated.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the claim that these are settled. Keep them open.**
  - No agreement has been reached through our authority process.
  - We should not assume unlimited liability, and we should not treat the issue as resolved.

---

## Summary and next steps

| Outcome | Issues |
|---|---|
| Reject / counter | 001–012, 014–016 |
| Hold pending information | 013 |
| Requires Amelia Frost written authority before any movement | 001 (20% cap), 003 (18 months), 009 (post-Completion release) |

**Immediate actions:**
1. Respond to the Seller that no position is agreed or final.
2. Issue our mark-up based on the playbook starting positions.
3. Request refreshed facts dated after 22 September 2026 on:
   - Bluefen consent and the cl 11.3 conditions;
   - the Riverlark payout figure;
   - bonus on-costs;
   - Ironquay payment confirmation;
   - DD-006 investigation status;
   - the Sandbar renewal terms.
4. Instruct title searches (ASIC, PPSR) independently of DD-012.
